reads.note: Screen does not call subscriptionApi.getSubscription() itself. PLANS[tier] (a local static table in src/types/subscription.ts, not fetched) is what actually drives the tier-picker card contents (price, split, slots) and is what a real backend's plan-catalog read must match. The success-screen 'Renews' date is a hardcoded literal '14 Aug 2027', not read from Subscription.renewsAt.

actions.name: subscribe

payload.name: tier
payload.source: user's tier-step selection, passed as the sole argument to subscriptionApi.subscribe(tier)

actions.note: SEAM-tagged in src/lib/api/subscription.ts as POST /api/hub/creator-subscription (tier=basic|pro). The mock's real side effect on success is NOT this call's return value -- the component ignores the resolved Subscription and instead calls the DEV-ONLY mock-session mutators setSubscriptionPaid(true) and setCreatorTier(tier) directly (see STUB-3). A real backend must make POST /api/hub/creator-subscription itself the thing that flips session.creator.subscriptionPaid and session.creator.tier server-side; nothing in this screen's code currently depends on the subscribe() response shape beyond it resolving successfully.

actions.name: setSubscriptionPaid (DEV ONLY)

payload.name: paid
payload.source: hardcoded true, called after subscribe() resolves

actions.note: Direct mutation of the in-memory mock session store (src/lib/api/mocks/session.ts), not an API call. STUB-1 and STUB-3. Must not exist against a real backend -- the real subscribe endpoint should be the sole source of this state change.

actions.name: setCreatorTier (DEV ONLY)

payload.name: tier
payload.source: the tier chosen in the tier step, called after subscribe() resolves

actions.note: Direct mutation of the in-memory mock session store. STUB-1 and STUB-3. Also mutates a derived field, slotsTotal (7 for pro, 3 for basic), that the real subscribe response would need to carry or that a session read would need to recompute.

authContext.note: The component itself performs no explicit auth or gate check (no creatorGates() call, no session read) -- it assumes it is only reachable by an already-authenticated user choosing to become a creator, and it writes session.creator fields on success as if that session already exists. It does not check accountType, canUpload, or kyc before rendering; it is presumably route-guarded upstream, but no such guard is present in this file.

special.note: The 'processing' step shows a fixed 62%-width progress bar (not driven by real progress events) for the duration of the subscribe() promise (700ms mock delay).

uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: initial step; also reached by pressing back from the tier step
user presses 'Choose a tier' on the value step, or 'Choose another tier' from the failed step
user presses 'Continue with {tier}' on the tier step
user presses 'Pay {price}' on the confirm step, calling pay() which sets step to 'processing' and awaits subscriptionApi.subscribe(tier)
subscriptionApi.subscribe(tier) resolves (mock always resolves after 700ms; no rejection path exists in the mock)

user taps the 'Simulate a failed payment' dev-only link on the confirm step -- there is no code path that reaches this state from an actual failed subscribe() call, because the mock subscribe() never rejects
uiStatesHandled.note: STUB-4. This is a dev-only preview trigger for the failure UI, not a reachable outcome of a real payment attempt in this codebase. A real backend must supply an actual failure response (e.g. declined charge) for this UI state to be reachable in production; currently nothing wires a real failure into step='failed'.
